newsitem.title: UK: UK's CDC to fund South Africa infrastructure via bonds.
newsitem.headline: UK's CDC to fund South Africa infrastructure via bonds.

text.p: The UK's Commonwealth Development Corp (CDC) is to participate in a company, INCA Finance, set up to finance infrastructure projects in South Africa via bond issues.

CDC, the UK's development finance institution, said INCA Finance will raise long term bonds in the South African market to offer to municipalities, water authorities and private infrastructure ventures.
The company aims to raise some 12 billion rand in the next seven years but will start with a capitalisation of 50 million rand in equity and 44 million rand in junior debt.

Shareholders in INCA Finance include CDC at 20 percent, First National Bank of South Africa 20 percent, Southern Life Ltd 10 percent, Future Growth Holdings Ltd 10 percent, Thebe Investments 10 percent, Old Mutual 5.0 percent and Women Investment Portfolio 5.0 percent.

INCA, which has a AA-minus rating from agency IBCA, will offer infrastructure providers with five, 10 and 15-year fixed rate debt financing, adding to the liquidity of the South African corporate debt market in the process.
South Africa's estimated infrastructure requirements will cost around 175 billion rand.

CDC said First National Bank (FNB) had played a major part in developing the financing initiative. FNB will be responsible along with South African merchant bank Msele for making a market in the bonds.
